newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors seek arrest of Hanbo founder.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors seek arrest of Hanbo founder.

text.p: A senior South Korean investigator said on Friday prosecutors were seeking the arrest of the founder of the troubled Hanbo Group over a loan scandal case.
"We will request an arrest warrant for Mr Chung Tae-soo within today," said Choi Byung-koog, head of the Central Investigation Department in charge of a probe into Hanbo.
Choi said Chung would be initially charged with illegally issuing cheques and violating the law on mutual trust and savings companies.
"All suspicions and allegations about him could be investigated once he is arrested," he told reporters.
State prosecutors summoned Chung from a Seoul hostpital on Thursday and have since questioned him over loans to Hanbo Steel, flagship of South Korea's 14th largest conglomerate.
They said they have questioned Chung on how the steelmaker secured five trillion won in loans from 61 creditors despite the company's shaky financial status.
